focus: popularity pruning, structured line families, point-line concentration, and near-lossless sampling

messages.body_markdown: Please supply a fresh exact proof of `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT`: from more than $\operatorname{wdeg}(C)$ simple compatible graph lines through one point, derive one $Q$ with $C\sim Z-Q$, then aggregate every disconnected $C$-class. Researcher-0003 P7 is audit-inexact, while researcher-0002 P8 only certifies the component-level decoder.
messages.subject: Factor linearization

messages.body_markdown: Proposed end-to-end interface: incidence supplies $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass and a rank-reaching relation degree $D=O_\eta(d)$. Then cleanup costs $O_\eta(d/p)=o(\epsilon)$ at the target threshold, and only $O_\eta(1)$ irreducible $Z$-factors remain. This preserves a constant fraction for one global polynomial and avoids Vinh below $p^{-1/2}$.
messages.subject: Near-linear interface

messages.body_markdown: The exact-audited balanced-color construction forces every cover reaching half of every accepted line to have $|R|=\Omega(p/\epsilon)$, despite an immediate constant decoder. Also, the accepted component inequalities with $\tau\ge k/(4p)$ cap support localization at exponent $1/2$. A near-linear route must therefore be algebra-aware sparsify-or-decode, not a universally smaller graph-only cover.
messages.subject: Graph-only ceiling

nodes.label: Accepted-incidence graph
nodes.notes: All measures use the uniform affine point-line incidence normalization.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $\mathcal L_p$ be the $p(p+1)$ affine lines of $\mathbb F_p^2$ and let $$E_{\rm acc}=\{(x,L):x\in L\text{ and }P_L(x)=f(x)\}.$$ Put $\epsilon=|E_{\rm acc}|/[p^2(p+1)]$ and $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)=\max_{\deg Q\le d}\Pr_x[Q(x)=f(x)].$$ For $G=(X,T,E)\subseteq E_{\rm acc}$ define $$e(G)=\frac{|E|}{p^2(p+1)},\quad \mu(G)=\frac{|X|}{p^2},\quad \tau(G)=\frac{|T|}{p(p+1)},\quad k(G)=\operatorname{mindeg}(G).$$

nodes.label: Rank-reaching line family
nodes.notes: This replaces cardinality control of $R$ by the actual rank of its labeled graph constraints.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $d\le D<p$, let $$V_D=\{A\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]:\operatorname{wdeg}_{(1,1,d)}A\le D\},\qquad N_d(D)=\dim V_D,$$ and $$\Phi_{R,D}:V_D\to\bigoplus_{M\in R}\mathbb F_p[t]_{\le D},\qquad A\mapsto\bigl(A(M(t),P_M(t))\bigr)_{M\in R}.$$ For $G=(X,T,E)$ set $$N_G(L)=\{x:(x,L)\in E\},$$ $$\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)=\{x\in N_G(L):\exists M\in R\setminus\{L\},\ (x,M)\in E\}.$$ The tuple $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching if $R\subseteq T$, $|R|>D$, $\operatorname{rank}\Phi_{R,D}<N_d(D)$, and $|\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)|>D$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Popularity pruning
nodes.notes: Exact source mapping; its compound source audit has verdict `revise`, so the harness determines status.
nodes.statement_markdown: If an accepted carrier has edge mass $\delta>0$ and line support at most $\sigma$, then for $k_0=\lfloor\delta p/100\rfloor$ it contains a subgraph $G_0$ with $$e(G_0)\ge\delta/4,\qquad k(G_0)\ge k_0,\qquad \delta/4\le\tau(G_0)\le\sigma.$$

nodes.label: Accepted component measures
nodes.notes: Mapped to the exact accepted component theorem input.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G=(X,T,E)$ be connected with minimum degree $k$, line measure $\tau$, and $C_*=2^{40}$. If $$k^2\ge C_*dp,\qquad k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2,$$ then $$\mu(G)\ge\frac{k}{4p},\qquad \tau\ge\frac{k}{4p}.$$

nodes.label: Component-sensitive reaching family
nodes.notes: The sampling proof loses only absolute constants.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-COMP-MEASURE`, writing $t=|T|$, there is $R\subseteq T$ such that $$\frac{4t}{k}\le |R|\le\frac{16t}{k}$$ and $$|\operatorname{Reach}_R(L)|>\frac12\deg_G(L)$$ for every $L\in T$. In particular, $|R|=\Theta(\tau p^2/k)$.

nodes.label: Standard explainer and extension
nodes.notes: This is the exact cardinality-based interpolation branch.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $r=|R|$ and $$D=16\bigl(\lfloor\sqrt{dr}\rfloor+1\bigr).$$ Under the component hypotheses there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ with $A_Z\not\equiv0$, $D/k<1/5000$, and $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ for every $L\in T$.

nodes.label: Standard simple-root core
nodes.notes: Content, resultant, peeling, and two-direction simplicity are kept as distinct source steps in the evidence list.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$ with $B$ primitive in $Z$. At most $pD^2+D|T|$ accepted edges are exceptional. Deleting them and peeling below $\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ leaves a nonempty graph $G_1$ of minimum degree at least $\lfloor k/100\rfloor$ such that $$B(x,f(x))=0,\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$$ at every point vertex.

nodes.label: Component-sensitive decoder
nodes.notes: The conclusion is one polynomial, not a list.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If a connected accepted component of minimum degree $k$ and line measure $\tau$ satisfies $$k^2\ge2^{40}dp,
\qquad k^3\ge2^{40}d\tau p^2,$$ then there is one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{k}{800p}.$$

nodes.label: Conditional square-root milestone
nodes.notes: The unproved antecedent is the existence of the small-line-measure component.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $G_0$ be a popularity core with minimum degree $k_0=\lfloor\epsilon p/100\rfloor$. If some component has $\tau\le\Lambda\epsilon$ and $$\epsilon\ge\sqrt{8{,}000{,}000\cdot2^{40}\Lambda}\left(\frac dp\right)^{1/2},$$ then one total-degree-at-most-$d$ polynomial satisfies $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge\frac{\epsilon}{160000}.$$

nodes.label: Support-localization ceiling
nodes.notes: Thus smaller component support within the existing cardinality/root-budget architecture cannot reach exponent $1-o(1)$.
nodes.statement_markdown: If $c\epsilon p\le k\le C\epsilon p$, $\tau\ge k/(4p)$, and $k^3\ge C_*d\tau p^2$, then $$\epsilon^2\ge\frac{C_*}{4C^2}\frac dp.$$

nodes.label: Universal-cover obstruction
nodes.notes: This obstructs graph-only sparsification, not soundness; the same table already has a constant decoder.
nodes.statement_markdown: For $p\ge103$ and $2\le K\le p/(100\log p)$ there is a legal table with $1/(2K)\le\epsilon\le2/K$ such that every $R$ reaching half of every accepted line satisfies $$|R|\ge\frac{Kp}{16}\ge\frac{p}{32\epsilon},$$ while some constant polynomial has agreement at least $\epsilon/2$.

nodes.label: Exact-linear endpoint
nodes.notes: The modal construction refutes this statement but remains below every fixed $(d/p)^{1-\eta}$ trigger. The compound source audit is `revise`.
nodes.statement_markdown: There are absolute $C,c>0$ such that, for all legal $p,d,f,P$, $$\epsilon\ge C\frac dp\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Rank-blind multiplicity barrier
nodes.notes: The snapshot has `audit_exact=false` and verdict `revise`; it is diagnostic only.
nodes.statement_markdown: In the regime $n>D$, uniform order-$s$ graph multiplicity certified solely by per-line jet codimension and transferred solely by $s$-fold root counting satisfies $$h^2>\frac{dn}{12}.$$

nodes.label: Low-weight sparsify-or-decode dichotomy
nodes.notes: This is the principal incidence obligation. `IE-L-COVER-OBSTRUCTION` requires the structured branch to exploit label-rank dependencies rather than merely reduce $|R|$.
nodes.statement_markdown:
For every $\eta>0$ there are $C_\eta,c_\eta,K_\eta>0$ such that, if $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta},$$ then either $\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c_\eta\epsilon$, or the popularity core contains an accepted subgraph $G$ for which there are $R$ and $D$ satisfying $$e(G)\ge c_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad d\le D\le K_\eta d,$$ and $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching.

nodes.label: Low-rank interpolation
nodes.notes: P3 supplies the squarefree and $Z$-dependence template; replacing its cardinality inequality by the stated rank inequality still needs an exact formalization.
nodes.statement_markdown:
If $(G,R,D)$ is rank-reaching, then there is a nonzero squarefree $A\in V_D$ such that $$A_Z\not\equiv0,
\qquad A(M(t),P_M(t))\equiv0$$ for every $M\in R$.

nodes.label: Reached-root extension
nodes.notes: The proof is ordinary degree-$D$ root counting and has no averaging loss.
nodes.statement_markdown: Under `IE-L-RANK-INTERP`, $$A(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$$ for every line vertex $L$ of $G$.

nodes.label: Exceptional-incidence count
nodes.notes: This exact count remains valid independently of how the low-rank interpolant was found.
nodes.statement_markdown: Write $A=HB$, where $H\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ is the coefficient content and $B$ is primitive in $Z$. Then $B$ is squarefree of degree below $p$, and there is a formal derivative $\mathcal D$ with $\gcd(B,\mathcal DB)=1$ such that the content, degenerate-line, and derivative-zero exceptional incidences satisfy $$|E_{\rm exc}|\le pD^2+D|T|.$$

nodes.label: Near-lossless cleanup at $D=O_\eta(d)$
nodes.notes: The new parameter substitution is $D/p\le K_\eta(d/p)\le(K_\eta/C_\eta)\epsilon$; it needs a fresh constant audit.
nodes.statement_markdown:
In the structured branch of `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY`, if $C_\eta$ is sufficiently large relative to $c_\eta,K_\eta$, exceptional deletion and popularity peeling leave a graph $G_1$ and $c'_\eta>0$ such that $$e(G_1)\ge c'_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad k(G_1)>D,$$ every line vertex satisfies $B(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$, and every point vertex satisfies $$B(x,f(x))=0,
\qquad B_Z(x,f(x))\ne0.$$

nodes.label: Bounded-factor concentration
nodes.notes: The cited factorwise source is pending and `audit_exact=false`; the node requires an exact proof in the current chain.
nodes.statement_markdown:
Factor $$B=c\prod_{i=1}^s C_i.$$ Then every $C_i$ depends on $Z$ and $$s\le\deg_ZB\le D/d\le K_\eta.$$ The simple-root graph partitions into factor classes. For some $C_i$ there is an accepted subgraph $F$ with $$e(F)\ge c''_\eta\epsilon,
\qquad k(F)>\operatorname{wdeg}(C_i),$$ such that $C_i(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line vertex and $C_{i,Z}(x,f(x))\ne0$ on every point vertex.

nodes.label: Factor linearization and global aggregation
nodes.notes: Researcher-0003 P7 is audit-inexact under a rejected compound submission; researcher-0002 P8 confirms component-level simple-root recovery but not this cross-component aggregation.
nodes.statement_markdown: Let $C\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y,Z]$ be irreducible with $\Delta=\operatorname{wdeg}(C)<p$. If an accepted factor class $F$ has minimum degree greater than $\Delta$, satisfies $C(L(t),P_L(t))\equiv0$ on every line vertex, and has $C_Z(x,f(x))\ne0$ at every point vertex, then there is $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ such that $$C\sim Z-Q$$ and $Q(x)=f(x)$ on every point vertex of $F$. Consequently, $$\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge e(F).$$

nodes.label: Close the sparsify-or-decode branches
nodes.notes: The direct branch is immediate; the structured branch uses only $O_\eta(1)$ factors and therefore loses an $\eta$-dependent constant, not a power of $d/p$.
nodes.statement_markdown: The dichotomy in `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` and lemmas `IE-L-RANK-INTERP` through `IE-L-FACTOR-LIFT` imply constants $C'_\eta,c'_\eta>0$ such that $$\epsilon\ge C'_\eta(d/p)^{1-\eta}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Agr}_d(f)\ge c'_\eta\epsilon.$$

nodes.label: Near-linear bivariate line-versus-point soundness
nodes.notes: Blocked principally on `IE-O-LOW-WEIGHT-DICHOTOMY` and a fresh exact audit of factor linearization. No roadmap work state is a proof-status claim.
nodes.statement_markdown: For every fixed $\eta>0$ there exist $C_\eta,c_\eta>0$ such that, for every prime $p$, every integer $100<d<p$, every $f:\mathbb F_p^2\to\mathbb F_p$, and every degree-at-most-$d$ affine-line table, $$\epsilon\ge C_\eta\left(\frac dp\right)^{1-\eta}$$ implies the existence of one $Q\in\mathbb F_p[X,Y]$ of total degree at most $d$ satisfying $$\Pr_{x\in\mathbb F_p^2}[Q(x)=f(x)]\ge c_\eta\epsilon.$$

summary: The exact corpus-mapped component chain gives a conditional exponent-$1/2$ decoder, while component support and universal cover arguments show that the same cardinality-based route cannot reach exponent $1-o(1)$. The proposed critical path replaces small $|R|$ by low labeled-constraint rank: preserve $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ accepted mass and obtain a relation of weighted degree $D=O_\eta(d)$. Then cleanup costs only $O_\eta(d/p)$, simple roots split the graph among $O_\eta(1)$ factors, and one factor can yield one global polynomial with $\Omega_\eta(\epsilon)$ agreement. The main open incidence node is the low-weight sparsify-or-decode dichotomy; factor linearization also needs a fresh exact proof audit.
target_statement: Convert local line-versus-point agreement into a structured affine-plane incidence configuration with only a $(d/p)^{o(1)}$ loss.
